title: Natural augmentation of standard sheaf cotangent complexes to differentials
statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space and $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Use the standard polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$ with augmentation $\epsilon$ and alternating complex $K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ of [lem-sfb-standard-sheaf-cotangent-flat-functorial-model]. Let $\Omega^1_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ be the sheafification of $U\mapsto\Omega^1_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$, with its universal derivation [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The degree-zero formula $\mathrm dp\otimes r\mapsto r\,\mathrm d(\epsilon p)$, and zero in negative degrees, defines a canonical chain map
$$\epsilon_\Omega:K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\longrightarrow\Omega^1_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}[0].$$
It induces an isomorphism $H^0(K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A})\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega^1_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$. More explicitly, before sheafification, for rings $A\to B$ on an open set, the cokernel of the first differential of $K_{B/A}$ is the $B$-module on symbols $\delta_b$ modulo
$$\delta_{\epsilon p}=\sum_b\epsilon(\partial p/\partial x_b)\delta_b\quad(p\in A[x_b\mid b\in B]).$$
These relations generate exactly the additivity, Leibniz and vanishing-on-$A$ relations, and the isomorphism sends $\delta_b$ to $\mathrm db$. The augmentation and its $H^0$ isomorphism are natural in all commutative squares of sheaves of rings and under continuous inverse image. For $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, the square consisting of the standard map $K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C\to K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}$, the two augmentations and the differential map commutes; the bottom map is $r\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto r\,\mathrm d(j(b))$, where $j:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ is the given map. No flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 08QF (lemma-identify-H0), 08UR (lemma-H0-L-morphism-sheaves-rings), and 08UV (lemma-H0-L-morphism-ringed-spaces), with the standard face calculation of Tag 08PN (definition-cotangent-complex-ring-map); sites-modules.tex Tags 08TP (lemma-differentials-sheafify) and 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials).

proof.text:
Work first with a ring map $A\to B$. In the standard construction of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], write $P_0=A[x_b\mid b\in B]$, $P_1=A[y_p\mid p\in P_0]$, and $\epsilon(x_b)=b$. The evaluation faces give $d_0(y_p)=p$ and $d_1(y_p)=x_{\epsilon(p)}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], $K^0$ is the free $B$-module on $\delta_b=\mathrm dx_b\otimes1$, and $K^{-1}$ is free on $\mathrm dy_p\otimes1$. Thus the alternating differential sends this latter basis element to
$$\sum_b\epsilon(\partial p/\partial x_b)\delta_b-\delta_{\epsilon(p)}.$$
Every sum is finite. Since $K^1=0$, $H^0(K)$ is precisely the cokernel of this map. Its relations are exactly the relations displayed in the statement.

source.place: Tags 08PM (definition-standard-resolution), 08PN (definition-cotangent-complex-ring-map); the evaluation faces are also written explicitly in simplicial.tex, example-polynomial-algebra-maps.

proof.text: The composite $P_0\xrightarrow{\epsilon}B\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\Omega_{B/A}$ is an $A$-derivation when the target is regarded as a $P_0$-module through $\epsilon$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] therefore gives a $B$-linear map $K^0\to\Omega_{B/A}$ with $\mathrm dp\otimes r\mapsto r\,\mathrm d(\epsilon p)$. For $t\in P_0$, the tensors $(t\,\mathrm dp)\otimes r$ and $\mathrm dp\otimes\epsilon(t)r$ both map to $r\epsilon(t)\,\mathrm d(\epsilon p)$, proving balancing explicitly. Its composites with the two faces on $\mathrm dy_p\otimes1$ are both $\mathrm d(\epsilon p)$, so it kills $d^{-1}$. Taking zero in all negative degrees makes a chain map to $\Omega_{B/A}[0]$. It sends $\delta_b$ to $\mathrm db$.

source.place: Tags 08PN (definition-cotangent-complex-ring-map) and 08QF (lemma-identify-H0), canonical differential map, computed here on the standard faces.

proof.text:
Let $F=\bigoplus_{b\in B}B\delta_b$, let $R_{\rm face}$ be the submodule generated by the relations in step 1, and let $R_{\rm der}$ be generated by the additive, product and base-ring relations in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Substituting $p=x_b+x_c$, $p=x_bx_c$, and the constant polynomial $p=a$ gives respectively
$$\delta_{b+c}-\delta_b-\delta_c,\qquad\delta_{bc}-b\delta_c-c\delta_b,\qquad\delta_{\varphi(a)}.$$
Each belongs to $R_{\rm face}$ (possibly with opposite sign). Hence $R_{\rm der}\subseteq R_{\rm face}$. These substitutions remain valid when labels coincide, including $b=c$ and rings of characteristic two.

source.place: Tag 07BK (definition-differentials), defining relation presentation; compared with the standard faces of cotangent.tex Tag 08PN.

proof.text:
Conversely, in $F/R_{\rm der}$ the assignment $D(b)=[\delta_b]$ is additive, satisfies $D(bc)=bD(c)+cD(b)$, and kills the image of $A$. For a monomial $p=a\prod_{i=1}^m x_{b_i}$, repeated Leibniz gives
$$D(\epsilon p)=\varphi(a)\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\prod_{j\ne i}b_j\right)D(b_i)=\sum_b\epsilon(\partial p/\partial x_b)D(b).$$
For $m=0$ both sides are zero; additivity gives the formula for every polynomial. Repeated labels contribute once for each occurrence, as do formal partial derivatives. Thus every face relation vanishes modulo $R_{\rm der}$, proving $R_{\rm face}\subseteq R_{\rm der}$. By the quotient description in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $F/R_{\rm face}=F/R_{\rm der}\cong\Omega_{B/A}$, with $[\delta_b]\mapsto\mathrm db$. This is exactly the map induced by step 2, so its $H^0$ map is an isomorphism. The monomial differentiation formula agrees with [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables].

source.place: Tags 07BK (definition-differentials), 00RO (lemma-universal-omega) and 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), with the explicit monomial calculation above.

proof.text: For $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ on $T$, apply steps 1--4 over each open $U$, with $A=\mathcal A(U)$ and $B=\mathcal B(U)$. Restricting coefficients and variable labels carries both faces and $\mathrm dp\otimes r\mapsto r\,\mathrm d(\epsilon p)$ to the same formulas on a smaller open; thus these are maps of presheaves. By [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison], sheafifying the sectionwise standard complex gives $K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$. By [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel], sheafifying the target gives $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ and its universal derivation. Sheafify the chain map. To identify $H^0$, use [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]: maps from the sheafification of the presheaf cokernel to any sheaf module $M$ are exactly maps from the degree-zero presheaf to $M$ killing its first differential. The same condition characterizes maps from the cokernel of the sheafified differential. These identifications are natural in $M$, so the two cokernels represent the same functor and are canonically isomorphic. The isomorphism is induced by sheafifying the presheaf cokernel map. Since the complexes have zero positive terms, this identifies $H^0(K)$ with the sheafification of the ring cokernels, and step 4 gives the required isomorphism. This argument takes cokernels of presheaves and then sheafifies; it does not assert that sheaf cokernels are sectionwise cokernels.

For a commutative square $(\mathcal A\to\mathcal B)\to(\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B')$ with upper coefficient map $\beta:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$, [lem-sfb-standard-sheaf-cotangent-flat-functorial-model] sends $\mathrm dp\otimes r$ to $\mathrm d(p')\otimes\beta(r)$ and has $\epsilon'(p')=\beta(\epsilon p)$. The induced differential map sends $\mathrm db$ to $\mathrm d(\beta b)$: this is defined by the universal derivation of [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel], since $b\mapsto\mathrm d(\beta b)$ is additive and Leibniz with coefficients restricted along $\beta$. Writing $\alpha:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ and $\varphi,\varphi'$ for the two structure maps, the square gives $\mathrm d(\beta(\varphi(a)))=\mathrm d(\varphi'(\alpha(a)))=0$, so this derivation kills $\mathcal A$. Both routes from degree zero to the target differentials therefore give
$$\beta(r)\,\mathrm d(\beta(\epsilon p)).$$
In negative degrees both give zero. This proves naturality of the chain augmentation, and passage to its degree-zero cokernel proves naturality of the $H^0$ isomorphism. Coefficients in the target are restricted along $\beta$ when comparing the maps.

source.place: Tag 08SS (definition-cotangent-complex-morphism-sheaves-rings and following commutative-square construction), together with sites-modules.tex Tag 08TP.

proof.text: Let $u:T'\to T$ be continuous. Take the sites of opens of $T$ and $T'$ in a common enlarged universe; their induced geometric morphism satisfies the small-site hypothesis of the differential comparison below. Use the inverse-image comparison of standard complexes from [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] and its compatibility with the standard maps in [lem-sfb-standard-sheaf-cotangent-flat-functorial-model]. Use [lem-trf-topos-inverse-image-differentials] for $u^{-1}\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\cong\Omega_{u^{-1}\mathcal B/u^{-1}\mathcal A}$, which preserves universal derivations. Under these comparisons the degree-zero augmentation is still the map induced by the derivation $p\mapsto\mathrm d(\epsilon p)$: the comparisons preserve the augmentation of the polynomial resolution and universal differentials. Thus its value on $\mathrm dp\otimes r$ is still $r\,\mathrm d(\epsilon p)$, while all negative components are zero. This proves compatibility of the chain maps with inverse image. By [lem-pc-inverse-image-module-functor-exact], continuous module inverse image preserves finite colimits. A cokernel is the coequalizer of a map and zero, so inverse image preserves the cokernel $H^0$ of these nonpositive complexes. Taking this cokernel gives precisely the asserted inverse-image compatibility of the $H^0$ isomorphism. Here the coefficient sheaf is $u^{-1}\mathcal B$; no additional scalar extension is being treated as exact.

source.place: Tag 08SV (lemma-pullback-cotangent-morphism-topoi); sites-modules.tex Tag 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials); sheaves.tex Tags 008X (lemma-pullback-module) and 008Y (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules).

proof.text: Finally take $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\xrightarrow{j}\mathcal C$. Tensor the first augmentation with $\mathcal C$ and use the standard chain map of [lem-sfb-standard-sheaf-cotangent-flat-functorial-model]. The bottom arrow $\mathcal C\otimes_{\mathcal B}\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\to\Omega_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}$ exists by the universal derivation in [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel]: $b\mapsto\mathrm d(jb)$ is an $\mathcal A$-derivation, so its linear extension sends $c\otimes\mathrm db$ to $c\,\mathrm d(jb)$. For a local section $b_0$ of $\mathcal B$, the tensors $c\,j(b_0)\otimes\mathrm db$ and $c\otimes b_0\mathrm db$ both map to $c\,j(b_0)\,\mathrm d(jb)$, so this extension is balanced over $\mathcal B$. On a local generator $(\mathrm dp\otimes r)\otimes c$, the route through $K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}$ gives $c\,j(r)\,\mathrm d(\epsilon' p')=c\,j(r)\,\mathrm d(j(\epsilon p))$. The route through $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$ gives the same expression. These elements generate degree zero locally, and every negative component of either route is zero. Hence the square commutes as a square of chain maps. Only linear maps and ordinary tensor products were used; exactness of scalar extension, and therefore flatness of $\mathcal C$ over $\mathcal B$, was never required.
